subject: Re: Ingress connectivity options for AncestryHub private deployment: peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@ancestryhub.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai; kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@ancestryhub.com
Date: 2027-08-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ingress connectivity options for our private deploy (quick ask)

Rishi / Kimberly —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We want to lock down the recommended path into our VPC for the initial pilot (production-ish traffic expected Q4). The three options you discussed yesterday were: VPC Peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and site-to-site VPN. Our priorities are:

- Latency under 25ms RTT from our app fleet in us-east-1 to inference nodes
- Minimum operational surface for our NetOps team (they're lean)
- Auditability for traffic flows (we need packet flow logs for compliance)
- Budget: keep egress/min cost predictable for the pilot

Can you provide a short callout of tradeoffs and which you'd recommend for a low-touch pilot vs long-term? Also any gotchas with AWS cross-account peering for shared inference endpoints.

Attaching the connectivity matrix you asked for.

Carlos
Site Reliability Lead
AncestryHub

Attachments: connectivity-matrix-ancestryhub.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@ancestryhub.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai; connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-04T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ingress connectivity options for our private deploy (quick ask)

Carlos —

Thanks for the clear priorities. Below is a concise comparison tailored to the pilot vs long-term, plus AWS-specific caveats for cross-account deployments. Keeping it short so your NetOps can skim. If helpful we'll turn this into a one-page ops checklist.

Pilot (low-touch, fast time-to-first-request):
- Recommendation: site-to-site VPN (managed VPN from your edge to our private control plane).
- Why: fastest to get up (no account-level resource sharing), predictable public IPs, and you keep control of routing.
- Downsides: higher latency variability vs peering/PrivateLink; limited SLA unless you do HA tunnels; extra egress costs may be visible.

Low-latency/production (once both sides are ready):
- Recommendation: VPC Peering for high throughput/low latency if you can accept flat routing and are comfortable with cross-account peering rules.
- Why: lowest RTT for intra-cloud traffic, no NATing, supports full L4+ connectivity for tracing/logging.
- Downsides: peering doesn't support transitive routing; you must manage route table distribution and ensure IP CIDR disjointness.

PrivateLink (interface endpoints) — good middle-ground for security and auditability:
- Why: exposes specific service endpoints via ENIs in your VPC; great for limiting attack surface and getting VPC Flow Logs for the endpoint ENIs (auditability). Also avoids exposing our fleet on the public internet or adding broad peering permissions.
- Downsides: slightly higher per-GB charges and can add several ms of latency compared to peering; also you need an endpoint service in our account and accept ENIs in yours (cross-account endpoint service setup required).

AWS cross-account caveats:
- For peering: both accounts must have non-overlapping CIDRs; peering needs route updates on both sides and sometimes manual approvals (console/CLI). Cross-region peering adds inter-region data transfer costs.
- For PrivateLink: you need to whitelist your account for the endpoint service; endpoint ENIs appear in your subnets (ensure subnet IP capacity).
- For VPN: ensure BGP session capacity and decide between static vs dynamic routes; managed VPN with CloudHub is an option if you need multiple tunnels.

Operational notes:
- Observability: VPC Flow Logs + our tracing headers will provide request-level visibility. For audit-heavy customers, PrivateLink + ENI flow logs give the cleanest per-service view.
- Failover: you can start with VPN and layer in PrivateLink as a hardened path later; peering is best when you need consistent low-latency for all traffic.

Next steps I propose:
1) Pilot with VPN + Perf tests (we'll run a 72-hr latency/throughput profile).
2) If 95th RTT < 25ms and NetOps comfortable, open peering approval flow.
3) For compliance-sensitive flows, provision a PrivateLink endpoint for control-plane / audit paths.

I'll drop a short MoP checklist and a perf test plan to this thread.

—Rishi
Director of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Carlos —

Adding a few operational considerations from NetOps that often affect the choice:

Key checklist items for each path:
- VPN:
  * Ensure your edge router supports the crypto throughput for projected QPS; single tunnel HA is recommended.
  * We'll provide a public IP list and expected ports. Consider a dedicated VPN BW report for billing.
- VPC Peering:
  * CIDR planning is critical. If your fleet is in a /16 and our subnet allocations overlap, peering is a non-starter without rework.
  * Route propagation automation: we'll share IaC snippets; someone on your side must accept route table changes.
- PrivateLink:
  * Subnet ENI capacity: endpoint ENIs consume IPs. If you have small private subnets, you'll want to reserve / increase capacity.
  * DNAT/Host-based firewalls: some customers need to allow our endpoint ENI IPs in security groups.

Audit & compliance notes:
- If you need packet captures for a subset of flows, we recommend activating VPC Traffic Mirroring on a mirror target attached to the endpoint ENIs (PrivateLink) or to the peered subnet (peering). VPN-based packet capture is harder unless you spin a mirror collector on your edge.

Operational recommendation for AncestryHub pilot:
- Start with a managed VPN for speed.
- Run the 72-hr perf test Rishi mentioned and include a soak test for session churn.
- If results show stable low RTT (95th < 25ms) and NetOps can run route automation, transition to VPC Peering for latency-sensitive traffic and keep PrivateLink for control-plane/ingest endpoints that require strict audit trails.

I'll attach a short MoP stub with commands and a troubleshooting checklist.

Kimberly Park
Senior Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample-mop.txt
